summary: dotenv-precheck postinstall harvests wallet seeds and.env secrets to Telegram
details: On install, package.json's postinstall runs index.js, an obfuscator.io-style bundle that walks the installer's project tree (from __dirname/../..) and user home directory, reads every.env* file, and scans file contents for BIP-39 mnemonics, 64-hex private keys, Solana keypair arrays, and environment assignments matching KEY|SECRET|TOKEN|PASSWORD|SEED|MNEMONIC|WALLET|CREDENTIAL. Harvested secrets are POSTed (and uploaded via sendDocument) to api.telegram.org using a hardcoded bot token whose URL is assembled from base64 fragments to hide the destination. The package's advertised 'dotenv preflight' purpose has no legitimate need to read wallet seed phrases, scan the user's home directory, or transmit data to a Telegram bot.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
